name: HTTP Request
category_description: Core node - built-in logic, data or generic API functionality
description: The HTTP Request node is one of the most versatile nodes in n8n. It allows you to make HTTP requests to query data from any app or service with a REST API. You can use the HTTP Request node as a regular node or attached to an AI agent to use as a tool{ data-preview }

parameters.name: Method
parameters.description: Select the method to use for the request:

parameters.name: URL
parameters.description: Enter the endpoint you want to use

parameters.name: Authentication
parameters.description: n8n recommends using the Predefined Credential Type option when it's available. It offers an easier way to set up and manage credentials, compared to configuring generic credentials

parameters.name: Predefined credentials
parameters.description: Credentials for integrations supported by n8n, including both built-in and community nodes. Use Predefined Credential Type for custom operations without extra setup. Refer to Custom API operations for more information

parameters.name: Generic credentials
parameters.description: Credentials for integrations not supported by n8n. You'll need to manually configure the authentication process, including specifying the required API endpoints, necessary parameters, and the authentication method

parameters.name: Send Query Parameters
parameters.description: Query parameters act as filters on HTTP requests. If the API you're interacting with supports them and the request you're making needs a filter, turn this option on
options: Using JSON: Enter JSON to define your query parameters

parameters.name: Send Headers
parameters.description: Use this parameter to send headers with your request. Headers contain metadata or context about your request
options: Using JSON: Enter JSON to define your header parameters

parameters.name: Send Body
parameters.description: If you need to send a body with your API request, turn this option on

parameters.name: Form URLencoded
parameters.description: Use this option to send your body as application/x-www-form-urlencoded

parameters.name: Form-Data
parameters.description: Use this option to send your body as multipart/form-data
options: Choose Form Data to enter Name/Value pairs
Choose n8n Binary File to pull the body from a file the node has access to
Name: Enter the ID of the field to set

parameters.name: JSON
parameters.description: Use this option to send your body as JSON
options: Using JSON: Enter JSON to define your body

parameters.name: n8n Binary File
parameters.description: Use this option to send the contents of a file stored in n8n as the body

parameters.name: Raw
parameters.description: Use this option to send raw data in the body
options: Body: Enter the raw body content to send

parameters.name: Array Format in Query Parameters
parameters.description: Use this option to control the format for arrays included in query parameters. Choose from these options:

parameters.name: Batching
parameters.description: Control how to batch large numbers of input items:
options: Items per Batch: Enter the number of input items to include in each batch

parameters.name: Ignore SSL Issues
parameters.description: By default, n8n only downloads the response if SSL certificate validation succeeds. If you'd like to download the response even if SSL certificate validation fails, turn this option on

parameters.name: Lowercase Headers
parameters.description: Choose whether to lowercase header names (turned on, default) or not (turned off)

parameters.name: Redirects
parameters.description: Choose whether to follow redirects (turned on by default) or not (turned off). If turned on, enter the maximum number of redirects the request should follow in Max Redirects

parameters.name: Response
parameters.description: Use this option to set some details about the expected API response, including:
options: JSON: Select this option to format the response as JSON

parameters.name: Pagination
parameters.description: Use this option to paginate results, useful for handling query results that are too big for the API to return in a single call

parameters.name: Proxy
parameters.description: Use this option if you need to specify an HTTP proxy

parameters.name: Timeout
parameters.description: Use this option to set how long the node should wait for the server to send response headers (and start the response body). The node aborts requests that exceed this value for the initial response

operation_details.summary: This error displays when the node reaches a host on the network but the target port has no listener. The TCP connection is actively refused. It isn't a DNS failure, a timeout, or a firewall drop

parameters.name: Target on the host machine, Docker Desktop (Mac or Windows)
parameters.description: use http://host.docker.internal: in the URL field. Docker Desktop adds this hostname automatically

parameters.name: Target on the host machine, Linux
parameters.description: pass --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway to the container, or set extra_hosts in docker-compose.yml:

parameters.name: Target in another container on the same Compose stack
parameters.description: use the service name as the hostname, for example http://my-api:5000. Reference the container's internal port, not the published ports: mapping

common_issues.title: Bad request - please check your parameters
common_issues.summary: This error displays when the node receives a 400 error indicating a bad request. This error most often occurs because:

common_issues.title: The resource you are requesting could not be found
common_issues.summary: This error displays when the endpoint URL you entered is invalid

common_issues.title: Connection refused (ECONNREFUSED)
common_issues.summary: This error displays when the node reaches a host on the network but the target port has no listener. The TCP connection is actively refused. It isn't a DNS failure, a timeout, or a firewall drop

common_issues.title: JSON parameter need to be an valid JSON
common_issues.summary: This error displays when you've passed a parameter as JSON and it's not formatted as valid JSON

common_issues.title: Forbidden - perhaps check your credentials
common_issues.summary: This error displays when the node receives a 403 error indicating authentication failed

common_issues.title: 429 - The service is receiving too many requests from you
common_issues.summary: This error displays when the node receives a 429 error from the service that you're calling. This often means that you have hit the rate limits of that service. You can find out more on the Handling API rate limits page

common_issues.title: Your uploaded file arrives with the wrong file name
common_issues.summary: When you send a file with Body Content Type set to Form-Data, n8n takes the file name of the multipart/form-data part from the binary data, not from the Name field. Name sets the form field name only. If the binary data has no file name, n8n sends file

common_issues.title: Unsupported media type (415) when you send a file
common_issues.summary: This error displays when the API expects multipart/form-data but the request body isn't multipart

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: The request method to use

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The URL to make the request to

options.name: Predefined Credential Type
options.description: We've already implemented auth for many services so that you don't have to set it up manually

options.name: Generic Credential Type
options.description: Fully customizable. Choose between basic, header, OAuth2, etc.

parameters.name: googleApiWarning
parameters.displayName: Make sure you have specified the scope(s) for the Service Account in the credential

parameters.name: provideSslCertificatesNotice
parameters.displayName: Provide certificates in node's 'Credential for SSL Certificates' parameter

parameters.name: sendQuery
parameters.description: Whether the request has query params or not

parameters.name: sendHeaders
parameters.description: Whether the request has headers or not

parameters.name: sendBody
parameters.description: Whether the request has a body or not

parameters.name: contentType
parameters.description: Content-Type to use to send body parameters

parameters.name: specifyBody
parameters.description: The body can be specified using explicit fields (keypair) or using a JavaScript object (json)

parameters.name: inputDataFieldName
parameters.description: The name of the incoming field containing the binary file data to be processed

options.name: allowUnauthorizedCerts
options.description: Whether to download the response even if SSL certificate validation is not possible

options.name: timeout
options.description: Time in ms to wait for the server to send response headers (and start the response body) before aborting the request

options.name: sendCredentialsOnCrossOriginRedirect
options.description: Whether to send credentials, like the "Authorization" header, on redirects to a different origin

parameters.name: optimizeResponse
parameters.description: Whether the optimize the tool response to reduce amount of data passed to the LLM that could lead to better result and reduce cost

parameters.name: dataField
parameters.description: Specify the name of the field in the response containing the data

parameters.name: fieldsToInclude
parameters.description: What fields response object should include

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of the field names. Supports dot notation. You can drag the selected fields from the input panel.

parameters.name: cssSelector
parameters.description: Select specific element(e.g. body) or multiple elements(e.g. div) of chosen type in the response HTML.

parameters.name: onlyContent
parameters.description: Whether to return only content of html elements, stripping html tags and attributes

parameters.name: elementsToOmit
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of selectors that would be excluded when extracting content

parameters.name: infoMessage
parameters.displayName: You can view the raw requests this node makes in your browser's developer console
